items.notes: On is pronounced exactly like ont, so context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Elle est allée au café avec sa sœur.
items.en: She went to the café with her sister.
items.ipa: /ɛl ɛ.t‿a.le o ka.fe a.vɛk sa sœʁ/
items.notes: Allée takes an extra silent e to agree with the feminine subject elle.

items.fr: Nous avons trouvé la tarte délicieuse.
items.notes: Trouvé stays masculine here because the direct object comes after the verb.

items.fr: Les cafés qu'elle a commandés étaient froids.
items.en: The coffees she ordered were cold.
items.ipa: /le ka.fe kɛl a kɔ.mɑ̃.de e.tɛ fʁwa/
items.notes: Commandés adds a silent s to agree with cafés, placed before the verb.

items.fr: Il va payer l'addition tout à l'heure.
items.en: He is going to pay the bill in a moment.
items.notes: À in tout à l'heure needs its accent, unlike the verb form a.

items.fr: Nous avons discuté ou nous avons juste bu un café.
items.en: We chatted, or we just had a coffee.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dis.ky.te u nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʒyst by œ̃ ka.fe/
items.notes: Ou without an accent means or, while où with an accent means where.

items.fr: Elle a demandé où se trouvaient les toilettes.
items.en: She asked where the restrooms were.
items.ipa: /ɛl a də.mɑ̃.de u sə tʁu.vɛ le twa.lɛt/
items.notes: Où keeps its accent because it means where, unlike the conjunction ou.

items.fr: Nous avons partagé l'addition à la fin du repas.
items.en: We split the bill at the end of the meal.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ paʁ.ta.ʒe la.di.sjɔ̃ a la fɛ̃ dy ʁə.pa/
items.notes: Partagé is distinguished from partager only by spelling, not by sound.

items.fr: Elle a acheté deux croissants qu'elle a partagés avec moi.
items.en: She bought two croissants that she shared with me.
items.ipa: /ɛl a aʃ.te dø kʁwa.sɑ̃ kɛl a paʁ.ta.ʒe a.vɛk mwa/
items.notes: Partagés takes a silent s to agree with the plural croissants placed earlier in the sentence.

items.fr: Il faut que tu viennes au café avec nous.
items.en: You need to come to the café with us.
items.ipa: /il fo kə ty vjɛn o ka.fe a.vɛk nu/
items.notes: Viennes in the subjunctive is pronounced with an audible n, unlike the indicative vient.

items.fr: Je ne pense pas qu'il finisse son café à temps.
items.en: I don't think he will finish his coffee in time.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kil fi.nis sɔ̃ ka.fe a tɑ̃/
items.notes: Finisse in the subjunctive is spelled with a double s, unlike the indicative finit.

items.fr: C'est le café où nous nous sommes rencontrés.
items.en: This is the café where we met.
items.ipa: /sɛ lə ka.fe u nu nu sɔm ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe/
items.notes: Rencontrés agrees with the plural subject nous, adding a silent s.

items.fr: Ce serveur est plus rapide que celui d'hier.
items.en: This waiter is faster than yesterday's.
items.ipa: /sə sɛʁ.vœʁ ɛ ply ʁa.pid kə sə.lɥi djɛʁ/
items.notes: Ce before a noun is a demonstrative, not to be confused with the pronoun se.

items.fr: Elle se demande si le café est encore ouvert.
items.en: She wonders if the café is still open.
items.ipa: /ɛl sə də.mɑ̃d si lə ka.fe ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ u.vɛʁ/
items.notes: Se before the verb is a reflexive pronoun, unlike the demonstrative ce.

items.fr: Ces cafés coûtent plus cher que ses habitudes ne le permettent.
items.en: These coffees cost more than his habits allow.
items.ipa: /se ka.fe kut ply ʃɛʁ kə se a.bi.tyd nə lə pɛʁ.mɛt/
items.notes: Ces, ses and c'est are all pronounced the same but never interchangeable in writing.

items.fr: C'est le meilleur café du quartier.
items.en: It's the best café in the neighborhood.
items.notes: C'est contracts cela est and sounds exactly like ces and ses.

items.fr: Quel café préfères-tu, celui-ci ou celui-là.
items.en: Which coffee do you prefer, this one or that one.
items.ipa: /kɛl ka.fe pʁe.fɛʁ ty sə.lɥi.si u sə.lɥi.la/
items.notes: Quel agrees with the masculine noun café, unlike the feminine form quelle.

items.en: Which terrace do you prefer in summer.
items.notes: Quelle takes the extra silent e to agree with the feminine noun terrasse.

items.fr: Bien qu'il soit tard, le café reste ouvert.
items.en: Although it is late, the café stays open.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa taʁ lə ka.fe ʁɛst u.vɛʁ/
items.notes: Soit is the subjunctive of être and must not be confused with the word soi.

items.fr: Je doute que ce serveur se souvienne de notre commande.
items.en: I doubt this waiter remembers our order.
items.ipa: /ʒə dut kə sə sɛʁ.vœʁ sə su.vjɛn də nɔtʁ kɔ.mɑ̃d/
items.notes: Se souvienne uses the subjunctive with an audible final n, unlike se souvient.

items.fr: Les clients ont attendu longtemps avant qu'on les serve.
items.en: The customers waited a long time before they were served.
items.ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ ɔ̃.t‿a.tɑ̃.dy lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ kɔ̃ le sɛʁv/
items.notes: Serve in the subjunctive drops the final t found in the indicative form sert.

items.fr: C'est la première fois qu'elle vient dans ce café.
items.en: It's the first time she has come to this café.
items.ipa: /sɛ la pʁə.mjɛʁ fwa kɛl vjɛ̃ dɑ̃ sə ka.fe/
items.notes: C'est here cannot be replaced by ses or ces, even though all three sound alike.

items.fr: Il semble que les prix aient encore augmenté.
items.en: It seems that prices have gone up again.
items.ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə le pʁi ɛ.t‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ o.gmɑ̃.te/
items.notes: Aient, the plural subjunctive of avoir, is pronounced just like the singular ait.

items.fr: Nous aimerions nous asseoir en terrasse, si cela ne vous dérange pas.
items.en: We would like to sit on the terrace, if that doesn't bother you.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿ɛ.mə.ʁjɔ̃ nu.z‿a.swaʁ ɑ̃ tɛ.ʁas si sə.la nə vu de.ʁɑ̃ʒ pa/
items.notes: Aimerions in the conditional needs a liaison right after nous.

items.fr: Quelles que soient ses habitudes, il commande toujours la même chose.
items.en: Whatever his habits are, he always orders the same thing.
items.ipa: /kɛl kə swa.t se a.bi.tyd il kɔ.mɑ̃d tu.ʒuʁ la mɛm ʃoz/
items.notes: Ses here is a possessive pronoun, not to be confused with c'est or ces.

items.fr: Il est possible que le serveur ait oublié notre commande.
items.en: It is possible that the waiter forgot our order.
items.ipa: /il ɛ pɔ.sibl kə lə sɛʁ.vœʁ ɛ.t‿u.bli.je nɔtʁ kɔ.mɑ̃d/
items.notes: Ait, the subjunctive of avoir, sounds exactly like the noun est or the verb es.

items.fr: Bien que ce café soit cher, il reste toujours plein.
items.en: Although this café is expensive, it is always full.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə sə ka.fe swa ʃɛʁ il ʁɛst tu.ʒuʁ plɛ̃/
items.notes: Ce before café is the demonstrative adjective, unlike the pronoun se in reflexive verbs.

items.fr: Les touristes ne savent pas quels cafés sont les plus authentiques.
items.en: The tourists don't know which cafés are the most authentic.
items.ipa: /le tu.ʁist nə sav pa kɛl ka.fe sɔ̃ le plyz‿o.tɑ̃.tik/
items.notes: Quels agrees with the plural masculine cafés, adding a silent s.

items.fr: Il faut absolument que nous choisissions une table à l'ombre.
items.en: We absolutely need to choose a table in the shade.
items.ipa: /il fo.t‿ab.sɔ.ly.mɑ̃ kə nu ʃwa.zi.sjɔ̃ yn tabl a lɔ̃bʁ/
items.notes: Choisissions in the subjunctive adds an extra syllable not heard in the indicative form.

items.fr: Il mélange la farine et les oeufs frais.
items.en: He mixes the flour and the fresh eggs.
items.ipa: /il melɑ̃ʒ la faʁin e lez‿ø fʁɛ/
items.notes: Les oeufs needs the z liaison from les even though oeufs itself starts with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Je coupe les oignons pour la soupe.
items.en: I cut the onions for the soup.
items.notes: The liaison between les and oignons adds a z sound that is easy to miss when writing.

items.fr: Elle épluche les carottes avec un couteau.
items.en: She peels the carrots with a knife.
items.ipa: /ɛl eplyʃ le kaʁɔt avɛk œ̃ kuto/
items.notes: The plural s on carottes is completely silent, so listen for les to know it is plural.

items.fr: Nous mangeons du pain frais chaque matin.
items.en: We eat fresh bread every morning.
items.ipa: /nu mɑ̃ʒɔ̃ dy pɛ̃ fʁɛ ʃak matɛ̃/
items.notes: Pain and matin both end in the nasal vowel in, which has no separate n sound to write out.

items.fr: Il boit un café sans sucre.
items.notes: Sans sounds exactly like sang and cent, so rely on meaning to spell it correctly.

items.fr: Tu manges une pomme à midi.
items.en: You eat an apple at noon.
items.notes: The preposition à sounds identical to the verb form a, but only one has an accent.

items.fr: Les enfants aiment les pâtes au fromage.
items.en: The children like pasta with cheese.
items.notes: Les enfants is joined by a z liaison that must not be forgotten in writing.

items.fr: Le chef prépare un plat délicieux.
items.en: The chef prepares a delicious dish.
items.notes: The final t of plat is never pronounced, which often leads learners to drop it in spelling too.

items.fr: Nous achetons des ananas au marché.
items.en: We buy pineapples at the market.
items.notes: Des ananas carries a z liaison from des that links smoothly into the vowel of ananas.

items.fr: Elle met un peu de sel dans la soupe.
items.en: She puts a little salt in the soup.
items.ipa: /ɛl mɛ œ̃ pø də sɛl dɑ̃ la sup/
items.notes: The verb met and the noun mets, meaning a dish, sound the same, so context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Il coupe le pain en tranches fines.
items.en: He cuts the bread into thin slices.
items.ipa: /il kup lə pɛ̃ ɑ̃ tʁɑ̃ʃ fin/
items.notes: En and tranches both use nasal vowels that have no audible n or m to copy down.

items.fr: Je fais cuire le riz dans l'eau chaude.
items.en: I cook the rice in hot water.
items.ipa: /ʒə fɛ kɥiʁ lə ʁi dɑ̃ lo ʃod/
items.notes: La eau is impossible to say, so la elides to l' before the vowel of eau.

items.fr: Les oeufs sont dans le réfrigérateur.
items.en: The eggs are in the refrigerator.
items.notes: Unlike singular un oeuf where the f is heard, the f and s of plural oeufs both stay silent.

items.fr: Tu bois de l'eau avec ton repas.
items.en: You drink water with your meal.
items.ipa: /ty bwa də lo avɛk tɔ̃ ʁəpa/
items.notes: De drops its e before the vowel in eau, becoming de l'eau.

items.fr: Nous préparons le dîner ensemble ce soir.
items.en: We are preparing dinner together tonight.
items.ipa: /nu pʁepaʁɔ̃ lə dine ɑ̃sɑ̃bl sə swaʁ/
items.notes: Dîner keeps a circumflex accent on the i even though it does not change the sound.

items.fr: Elle achète des fruits frais tous les jours.
items.en: She buys fresh fruit every day.
items.ipa: /ɛl aʃɛt de fʁɥi fʁɛ tu le ʒuʁ/
items.notes: Before a consonant, tous drops its final s sound, unlike when it stands alone.

items.fr: Les tomates sont mûres et rouges.
items.en: The tomatoes are ripe and red.
items.notes: Sont is a homophone of son, so only the sentence meaning tells them apart.

items.fr: Je goûte la sauce avant de servir.
items.en: I taste the sauce before serving.
items.ipa: /ʒə gut la sos avɑ̃ də sɛʁviʁ/
items.notes: Goûte keeps its circumflex accent on the u, a spelling detail invisible in speech.

items.fr: Vous mangez du poulet rôti ce soir.
items.en: You are eating roast chicken tonight.
items.ipa: /vu mɑ̃ʒe dy pulɛ ʁoti sə swaʁ/
items.notes: The final t of poulet is always silent, like most words ending in -et.

items.fr: Elle lave les fraises dans l'évier.
items.en: She washes the strawberries in the sink.
items.notes: La évier cannot be said aloud, so la becomes l' before the vowel.

items.fr: Il ajoute du poivre sur la viande.
items.en: He adds pepper to the meat.
items.ipa: /il aʒut dy pwavʁ syʁ la vjɑ̃d/
items.notes: Sur, meaning on, and sûr, meaning certain, sound identical, only the accent tells them apart in writing.

items.fr: Nous cuisinons ensemble le dimanche matin.
items.en: We cook together on Sunday morning.
items.notes: Ensemble and dimanche both hide nasal vowels with no separate n or m sound.

items.fr: Ils mangent des légumes verts chaque soir.
items.en: They eat green vegetables every evening.
items.ipa: /il mɑ̃ʒ de legym vɛʁ ʃak swaʁ/
items.notes: Mangent sounds exactly like the singular mange, so only the subject ils signals the plural.

items.fr: Je prends deux oeufs pour l'omelette.
items.en: I take two eggs for the omelette.
items.notes: La omelette is not possible to pronounce, so it becomes l'omelette.

items.fr: Le pain sent bon dans la cuisine.
items.en: The bread smells good in the kitchen.
items.ipa: /lə pɛ̃ sɑ̃ bɔ̃ dɑ̃ la kɥizin/
items.notes: Pain, sent and bon all rely on nasal vowels that leave no separate letter to hear.

items.fr: Elle sert la soupe très chaude.
items.en: She serves the soup very hot.
items.notes: The t at the end of sert is silent, so it is easy to forget when spelling the verb.

items.fr: Il verse l'huile dans la poêle.
items.en: He pours the oil into the pan.
items.notes: La huile is never said, la elides to l' before this vowel sound.

items.fr: Je ne mange pas de fromage.
items.notes: The mute e in je and ne is barely heard, so both words are easy to run together when writing.

items.fr: Elle achète du beurre frais pour la tarte.
items.en: She buys fresh butter for the pie.
items.ipa: /ɛl aʃɛt dy bœʁ fʁɛ puʁ la taʁt/
items.notes: Achète needs a grave accent on the e to keep the open sound, unlike acheter.

items.fr: Nous buvons un jus de fruits ensemble.
items.en: We drink a fruit juice together.
items.ipa: /nu byvɔ̃ œ̃ ʒy də fʁɥi ɑ̃sɑ̃bl/
items.notes: Un and ensemble both carry nasal vowels with no separate consonant sound to spell.

items.fr: Les invités arrivent pour le déjeuner.
items.notes: Les invités is joined by a z liaison since invités starts with a vowel sound.

items.fr: Je range les assiettes dans le placard.
items.en: I put the plates away in the cupboard.
items.notes: Les assiettes links with a z sound from les before the vowel of assiettes.

items.fr: Elle choisit un gâteau au chocolat.
items.notes: Gâteau keeps its circumflex accent on the a, a silent spelling clue.

items.fr: Tu manges trop de bonbons aujourd'hui.
items.en: You are eating too many candies today.
items.notes: Aujourd'hui is itself a frozen elision of au jour de hui and must be written as one word with an apostrophe.

items.fr: Les voisins cuisinent un plat traditionnel pour la fête.
items.en: The neighbors are cooking a traditional dish for the celebration.
items.ipa: /le vwazɛ̃ kɥizin œ̃ pla tʁadisjɔnɛl puʁ la fɛt/
items.notes: Cuisinent sounds just like the singular cuisine, so only les voisins shows it is plural.

items.fr: Je bois un jus d'orange le matin.
items.en: I drink orange juice in the morning.
items.ipa: /ʒə bwa œ̃ ʒy dɔʁɑ̃ʒ lə matɛ̃/
items.notes: Un and matin both end in nasal vowels that hide any separate n sound.

items.fr: Elle a acheté des tomates au marché.
items.en: She bought tomatoes at the market.
items.ipa: /ɛl a aʃte de tɔmat o maʁʃe/
items.notes: The auxiliary a and the preposition à sound identical, only the accent marks the difference.

items.fr: Nous avons mangé une pizza délicieuse.
items.notes: Mangé, manger and mangez are all pronounced the same way, so grammar must decide the ending.

items.fr: Il va préparer le dîner ce soir.
items.en: He is going to prepare dinner tonight.
items.ipa: /il va pʁepaʁe lə dine sə swaʁ/
items.notes: The final r of the infinitive préparer is never pronounced.

items.fr: Nous allons faire les courses ce matin.
items.en: We are going to do the grocery shopping this morning.
items.notes: Nous allons links with a z liaison before the vowel of allons.

items.fr: Elle a mis la table avant le repas.
items.en: She set the table before the meal.
items.ipa: /ɛl a mi la tabl avɑ̃ lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The past participle mis ends in a silent s that is often forgotten in dictation.

items.fr: Ils ont mangé toutes les crêpes.
items.notes: Ont and on sound exactly the same, so only context shows which one is meant.

items.fr: On a préparé un gâteau pour son anniversaire.
items.en: We made a cake for his birthday.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ a pʁepaʁe œ̃ gato puʁ sɔ̃n‿anivɛʁsɛʁ/
items.notes: On is easily confused with ont since both are pronounced the same nasal sound.

items.en: Where did you buy this cheese?
items.notes: Où, meaning where, and ou, meaning or, are pronounced identically, only the accent separates them.

items.fr: Tu vas éplucher les pommes de terre.
items.en: You are going to peel the potatoes.
items.ipa: /ty va eplyʃe le pɔm də tɛʁ/
items.notes: The final r of éplucher stays silent, as in every -er infinitive.

items.fr: Elle a fait cuire les pâtes dix minutes.
items.en: She cooked the pasta for ten minutes.
items.ipa: /ɛl a fɛ kɥiʁ le pat di minyt/
items.notes: The irregular past participle fait ends in a silent t.

items.fr: Nous avons goûté la sauce avant de la servir.
items.en: We tasted the sauce before serving it.
items.ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ gute la sos avɑ̃ də la sɛʁviʁ/
items.notes: Goûté still carries the circumflex accent from goûter, even in the past participle.

items.fr: Les enfants ont bu tout le jus d'orange.
items.en: The children drank all the orange juice.
items.ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ ɔ̃ by tu lə ʒy dɔʁɑ̃ʒ/
items.notes: Enfants liaises into ont with a hidden z sound that must still be written as two words.

items.fr: Elle va couper les carottes en rondelles.
items.en: She is going to cut the carrots into rounds.
items.ipa: /ɛl va kupe le kaʁɔt ɑ̃ ʁɔ̃dɛl/
items.notes: Like all -er infinitives, couper ends in a completely silent r.

items.fr: J'ai lavé la salade avant de la manger.
items.en: I washed the salad before eating it.
items.ipa: /ʒe lave la salad avɑ̃ də la mɑ̃ʒe/
items.notes: Lavé, laver and lavez all sound the same, so the ending must be chosen by grammar, not by ear.

items.fr: Nous avons acheté des pommes et des poires.
items.notes: Avons acheté chains two liaisons in a row that are easy to miss in fast speech.

items.fr: Il a versé l'huile dans la poêle chaude.
items.en: He poured the oil into the hot pan.
items.ipa: /il a vɛʁse lɥil dɑ̃ la pwal ʃod/
items.notes: La huile is unpronounceable, so it becomes l'huile before the vowel sound.

items.fr: Elle a préparé la soupe qu'elle a servie chaude.
items.en: She made the soup she served hot.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pʁepaʁe la sup kɛl a sɛʁvi ʃod/
items.notes: Servie is pronounced exactly like servi, but the silent added e agrees with the feminine soupe.

items.fr: On va manger dans la cuisine ce soir.
items.en: We are going to eat in the kitchen tonight.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ va mɑ̃ʒe dɑ̃ la kɥizin sə swaʁ/
items.notes: On here is easy to confuse with ont since both share the same nasal sound.

items.fr: Les invités sont arrivés avant le dîner.
items.notes: With être, arrivés adds a silent s to agree with the plural invités.

items.fr: Elle a coupé les légumes qu'elle a lavés ce matin.
items.en: She cut the vegetables she washed this morning.
items.ipa: /ɛl a kupe le legym kɛl a lave sə matɛ̃/
items.notes: Lavés sounds identical to lavé, but the silent s agrees with the plural légumes.

items.fr: Il faut que nous mangions des légumes variés chaque jour.
items.en: We must eat varied vegetables every day.
items.ipa: /il fo kə nu mɑ̃ʒjɔ̃ de legym vaʁje ʃak ʒuʁ/
items.notes: Before the ending -ions, -ger verbs like manger drop the extra e since the following i already softens the g.

items.fr: Je ne pense pas que ce plat soit trop épicé.
items.en: I do not think this dish is too spicy.
items.ipa: /ʒə nə pɑ̃s pa kə sə pla swa tʁo epise/
items.notes: Ce, meaning this, and se, the reflexive pronoun, are pronounced exactly the same way.

items.fr: Ces épices viennent du marché, mais ses habitudes culinaires ont changé.
items.en: These spices come from the market, but her cooking habits have changed.
items.ipa: /sez‿episɛ vjɛn dy maʁʃe mɛ sez‿abityd kylinɛʁ ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe/
items.notes: Ces and ses sound completely identical, so only grammar tells them apart.

items.fr: C'est la recette que ma grand-mère préférait.
items.en: This is the recipe my grandmother preferred.
items.ipa: /sɛ la ʁəsɛt kə ma gʁɑ̃mɛʁ pʁefeʁɛ/
items.notes: C'est sounds the same as ces and ses, so the apostrophe is the only visual clue.

items.fr: Quel plat préfères-tu pour le dîner de ce soir?
items.en: Which dish do you prefer for dinner tonight?
items.ipa: /kɛl pla pʁefɛʁ ty puʁ lə dine də sə swaʁ/
items.notes: Quel and quelle sound identical, so the ending must match the noun's gender in writing.

items.fr: Quelle sauce accompagne le mieux ce poisson grillé?
items.en: Which sauce goes best with this grilled fish?
items.ipa: /kɛl sos akɔ̃paɲ lə mjø sə pwasɔ̃ gʁije/
items.notes: Quelle sounds exactly like quel, so only the feminine noun sauce shows the correct spelling.

items.fr: Bien qu'il soit tard, elle continue à préparer le repas.
items.en: Although it is late, she keeps preparing the meal.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil swa taʁ ɛl kɔ̃tiny a pʁepaʁe lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The subjunctive soit ends in a silent t that is easy to drop by mistake.

items.fr: Il faudrait que vous ajoutiez un peu plus de sel.
items.en: You should add a little more salt.
items.ipa: /il fodʁɛ kə vuz‿aʒutje œ̃ pø ply də sɛl/
items.notes: The ending -iez is pronounced yé, which is easy to confuse with the simpler -ez ending.

items.fr: Elle doute que ce dessert soit vraiment sans sucre.
items.en: She doubts this dessert is really sugar free.
items.ipa: /ɛl dut kə sə desɛʁ swa vʁɛmɑ̃ sɑ̃ sykʁ/
items.notes: Sans sounds identical to sang and cent, so only context fixes the spelling.

items.fr: Les invités, bien qu'ils aient déjà mangé, reprennent du gâteau.
items.en: The guests, although they already ate, take more cake.
items.ipa: /lez‿ɛ̃vite bjɛ̃ kilz‿ɛ deʒa mɑ̃ʒe ʁəpʁɛn dy gato/
items.notes: The subjunctive aient is pronounced just like est, with the whole ending staying silent.

items.fr: Ce cuisinier ne se souvient plus de la recette exacte.
items.en: This cook no longer remembers the exact recipe.
items.ipa: /sə kɥizinje nə sə suvjɛ̃ ply də la ʁəsɛt ɛgzakt/
items.notes: Ce and se appear together here and sound completely identical.

items.fr: Mes parents pensent que ces légumes sont meilleurs que les surgelés.
items.en: My parents think these vegetables are better than frozen ones.
items.ipa: /me paʁɑ̃ pɑ̃s kə se legym sɔ̃ mɛjœʁ kə le syʁʒəle/
items.notes: Ces is a homophone of ses and c'est, easily mixed up while writing quickly.

items.fr: Il semble que les enfants aient adoré le repas.
items.en: It seems the children loved the meal.
items.ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃z‿ɛ adɔʁe lə ʁəpa/
items.notes: The liaison before aient sounds just like the liaison before ont, so the two are easy to confuse when writing.

items.fr: Je voudrais que tu choisisses un dessert pour ce soir.
items.en: I would like you to choose a dessert for tonight.
items.ipa: /ʒə vudʁɛ kə ty ʃwazis œ̃ desɛʁ puʁ sə swaʁ/
items.notes: The subjunctive choisisses is pronounced exactly like the indicative choisis, with the extra letters staying silent.

items.fr: Nous avons besoin d'un grand chef pour organiser ce banquet.
items.en: We need a great chef to organize this banquet.
items.ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ bəzwɛ̃ dœ̃ gʁɑ̃ ʃɛf puʁ ɔʁganize sə bɑ̃kɛ/
items.notes: De un is never said aloud, so it becomes d'un before the vowel.

items.fr: Ce dessert paraît trop sucré pour certains invités.
items.en: This dessert seems too sweet for some guests.
items.ipa: /sə desɛʁ paʁɛ tʁo sykʁe puʁ sɛʁtɛ̃z‿ɛ̃vite/
items.notes: Certains and invités both carry nasal vowels that hide any separate n sound before the liaison.

items.fr: Les grands chefs insistent pour que les ingrédients soient frais.
items.en: Great chefs insist that the ingredients be fresh.
items.ipa: /le gʁɑ̃ ʃɛfz‿ɛ̃sist puʁ kə lez‿ɛ̃gʁedjɑ̃ swat fʁɛ/
items.notes: The liaison after plural chefs is easy to mistake for the sound of a singular chef alone.

items.fr: Elle a l'habitude de goûter chaque plat avant qu'il ne soit servi.
items.en: She usually tastes every dish before it is served.
items.ipa: /ɛl a labityd də gute ʃak pla avɑ̃ kil nə swa sɛʁvi/
items.notes: La habitude cannot be pronounced, so it elides to l'habitude.

items.fr: Ses amis pensent que ce restaurant mérite trois étoiles.
items.en: Her friends think this restaurant deserves three stars.
items.ipa: /sez‿ami pɑ̃s kə sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ meʁit tʁwaz‿etwal/
items.notes: Ses sounds the same as ce and c'est, so only grammar reveals the right spelling.

items.fr: Il vaut mieux que nous réservions une table avant huit heures.
items.en: It is better that we reserve a table before eight o'clock.
items.ipa: /il vo mjø kə nu ʁezɛʁvjɔ̃ yn tabl avɑ̃ ɥit‿œʁ/
items.notes: The t of huit is silent alone but reappears in liaison before the vowel of heures.

items.fr: C'est étonnant que ces enfants aiment autant les épinards.
items.en: It is surprising that these children like spinach so much.
items.notes: C'est and ces are pronounced the same way, distinguishable only by their spelling and role.

items.fr: Quelles épices utilises-tu pour ce curry maison?
items.en: Which spices do you use for this homemade curry?
items.ipa: /kɛlz‿episɛ ytiliz ty puʁ sə kyʁi mɛzɔ̃/
items.notes: Quelles épices links with a z liaison that must still be spelled as two separate words.

items.fr: Bien que ce gâteau soit simple, il plaît à tout le monde.
items.en: Although this cake is simple, everyone likes it.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə sə gato swa sɛ̃pl il plɛ a tu lə mɔ̃d/
items.notes: Plaît keeps a circumflex accent on the i, a silent spelling detail carried over from plaire.

items.fr: Nous doutons que ses économies suffisent pour ce restaurant étoilé.
items.en: We doubt her savings are enough for this starred restaurant.
items.ipa: /nu dutɔ̃ kə sez‿ekɔnɔmi syfiz puʁ sə ʁɛstɔʁɑ̃ etwale/
items.notes: Ses is a classic homophone trap, sounding identical to ce and c'est.
Sont sounds like son; only the verb context tells you to add the final t.

items.fr: La cuisine est à côté du salon.
items.en: The kitchen is next to the living room.
items.notes: "à" (preposition, with accent) must not be confused with "a" (verb avoir), even though both sound the same.

items.fr: Il y a un grand lit dans la chambre.
items.en: There is a big bed in the bedroom.
items.ipa: /il i a œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃ li dɑ̃ la ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: The final "d" of "grand" and the final "t" of "lit" are both silent.

items.fr: Nous rangeons nos affaires chaque matin.
items.en: We put our things away every morning.
items.notes: Liaison links "nos" and "affaires" with a /z/ sound that has no letter of its own to add.

items.fr: Mon frère dort dans la petite chambre.
items.en: My brother sleeps in the small bedroom.
items.ipa: /mɔ̃ fʁɛʁ dɔʁ dɑ̃ la pə.tit ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: The final "e" of "petite" is silent, but it makes the preceding "t" audible, unlike masculine "petit".

items.fr: Le salon a deux fenêtres et une porte.
items.en: The living room has two windows and one door.
items.ipa: /lə sa.lɔ̃ a dø fə.nɛtʁ e yn pɔʁt/
items.notes: "et" (and) sounds exactly like "est" (is), so context alone tells you which spelling to use.

items.fr: Ma sœur balaie la cuisine tous les soirs.
items.en: My sister sweeps the kitchen every evening.
items.ipa: /ma sœʁ ba.lɛ la kɥi.zin tu le swaʁ/
items.notes: "balaie" keeps the "ai" spelling even though it sounds like a simple "è".

items.fr: Les rideaux sont bleus dans le salon.
items.en: The curtains are blue in the living room.
items.ipa: /le ʁi.do sɔ̃ blø dɑ̃ lə sa.lɔ̃/
items.notes: The final "x" of "rideaux" and the final "s" of "bleus" are both silent plural markers.

items.fr: Il ferme la fenêtre parce qu'il fait froid.
items.en: He closes the window because it is cold.
items.ipa: /il fɛʁm la fə.nɛtʁ paʁs.kil fɛ fʁwa/
items.notes: "que" drops its "e" before the vowel of "il", written as "qu'il".

items.fr: Nous avons un canapé confortable au salon.
items.en: We have a comfortable sofa in the living room.
items.notes: "Nous avons" is joined by a liaison /z/ even though "nous" ends in a silent "s".

items.fr: La salle de bain est au bout du couloir.
items.en: The bathroom is at the end of the hallway.
items.ipa: /la sal də bɛ̃ ɛ.t‿o bu dy ku.lwaʁ/
items.notes: "bain" is one single nasal sound, not "ba" plus a separate "n".

items.fr: Mes parents rangent le garage le samedi.
items.en: My parents tidy the garage on Saturdays.
items.ipa: /me pa.ʁɑ̃ ʁɑ̃ʒ lə ɡa.ʁaʒ lə sam.di/
items.notes: The "ent" ending of "rangent" is completely silent, just like most third person plural verb endings.

items.fr: On mange dans la cuisine ce soir.
items.en: We are eating in the kitchen tonight.
items.ipa: /ɔ̃ mɑ̃ʒ dɑ̃ la kɥi.zin sə swaʁ/
items.notes: "on" (we, one) sounds identical to "ont" (they have), so only sentence sense tells you which to write.

items.fr: Le chat dort sur le grand lit blanc.
items.en: The cat sleeps on the big white bed.
items.ipa: /lə ʃa dɔʁ syʁ lə ɡʁɑ̃ li blɑ̃/
items.notes: The final consonants of "grand" and "blanc" are silent unless a liaison occurs.

items.fr: J'ouvre la porte de la cave doucement.
items.en: I open the cellar door slowly.
items.ipa: /ʒuvʁ la pɔʁt də la kav dus.mɑ̃/
items.notes: "je" loses its "e" before a vowel and becomes "j'" attached to "ouvre".

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de bruit chez les voisins.
items.en: There is a lot of noise at the neighbors' place.
items.ipa: /il i a bo.ku də bʁɥi ʃe le vwa.zɛ̃/
items.notes: "beaucoup" combines the tricky spelling "eau" for /o/ with "ou" for /u/, easy to mix up when writing fast.

items.fr: Nous avons déménagé dans un nouvel appartement.
items.en: We moved into a new apartment.
items.notes: The past participle "déménagé" sounds identical to the infinitive "déménager", so the ending must be chosen from grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Elle a peint les murs du salon en bleu.
items.en: She painted the living room walls blue.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pɛ̃ le myʁ dy sa.lɔ̃ ɑ̃ blø/
items.notes: "peint" ends in a nasal sound with a silent final "t", an irregular past participle spelling.

items.fr: Nous allons repeindre la cuisine ce week-end.
items.en: We are going to repaint the kitchen this weekend.
items.notes: Liaison links "nous" and "allons" with a /z/ sound before the verb.

items.fr: Les voisins ont fait beaucoup de bruit hier soir.
items.en: The neighbors made a lot of noise last night.
items.ipa: /le vwa.zɛ̃ ɔ̃ fɛ bo.ku də bʁɥi jɛʁ swaʁ/
items.notes: "ont" (they have) sounds like "on", so check the plural subject "les voisins" to know it takes "ont".

items.fr: J'ai acheté des étagères pour la chambre.
items.en: I bought some shelves for the bedroom.
items.ipa: /ʒe aʃ.te de ze.ta.ʒɛʁ puʁ la ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "acheté" ends in the same sound as the infinitive "acheter", so only the auxiliary "ai" shows it is a past participle.

items.fr: Où as-tu rangé les clés de la maison?
items.en: Where did you put the house keys?
items.ipa: /u a ty ʁɑ̃.ʒe le kle də la mɛ.zɔ̃/
items.notes: "où" (where, with accent) must not be confused with "ou" (or), even though both sound the same.

items.fr: Ma mère a nettoyé toute la maison ce matin.
items.en: My mother cleaned the whole house this morning.
items.ipa: /ma mɛʁ a nɛ.twa.je tut la mɛ.zɔ̃ sə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: "nettoyé" stays masculine singular because the direct object "la maison" comes after the verb, not before.

items.fr: Ils vont poser un nouveau parquet dans le couloir.
items.en: They are going to lay new flooring in the hallway.
items.ipa: /il vɔ̃ po.ze œ̃ nu.vo paʁ.kɛ dɑ̃ lə ku.lwaʁ/
items.notes: The final "t" of "vont" is silent, and "parquet" also ends in a silent "t".

items.fr: Nous avons enfin fini les travaux de la salle de bain.
items.en: We have finally finished the bathroom renovations.
items.ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃.z‿ɑ̃.fɛ̃ fi.ni le tʁa.vo də la sal də bɛ̃/
items.notes: Two liaisons in a row link "nous avons" and "avons enfin" with /z/ sounds.

items.fr: Le propriétaire va augmenter le loyer en janvier.
items.en: The landlord is going to raise the rent in January.
items.ipa: /lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ va oɡ.mɑ̃.te lə lwa.je ɑ̃ ʒɑ̃.vje/
items.notes: "en" before a consonant makes a nasal sound with no separate "n" pronounced.

items.fr: Elle a déjà fini de ranger sa chambre.
items.en: She has already finished tidying her room.
items.ipa: /ɛl a de.ʒa fi.ni də ʁɑ̃.ʒe sa ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "déjà" always keeps its grave accent on the final "a" even though nothing in the pronunciation signals it.

items.fr: Il faut que tu fasses le ménage ce week-end.
items.en: You need to do the housework this weekend.
items.ipa: /il fo kə ty fas lə me.naʒ sə wik.ɛnd/
items.notes: The subjunctive "fasses" replaces the indicative "fais" after "il faut que", an irregular form of "faire".

items.fr: Ces meubles ne sont pas très solides.
items.en: These pieces of furniture are not very sturdy.
items.ipa: /se mœbl nə sɔ̃ pa tʁɛ sɔ.lid/
items.notes: "ces" (these, demonstrative) sounds exactly like "ses" (his/her) and "c'est" (it is).

items.fr: Je pense que ce logement est trop cher pour nous.
items.en: I think this place is too expensive for us.
items.ipa: /ʒə pɑ̃s kə sə lɔʒ.mɑ̃ ɛ tʁo ʃɛʁ puʁ nu/
items.notes: "ce" (this, demonstrative adjective) is easily confused with the reflexive pronoun "se", even though no reflexive verb appears here.

items.fr: Quelle chambre préfères-tu, la grande ou la petite?
items.en: Which bedroom do you prefer, the big one or the small one?
items.ipa: /kɛl ʃɑ̃bʁ pʁe.fɛʁ ty la ɡʁɑ̃d u la pə.tit/
items.notes: "quelle" agrees in the feminine with "chambre" and sounds identical to "quel", "quels", and "quelles".

items.fr: Bien qu'il pleuve, nous devons réparer le toit aujourd'hui.
items.en: Even though it is raining, we have to repair the roof today.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kil plœv nu də.vɔ̃ ʁe.pa.ʁe lə twa o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
items.notes: "pleuve" is the irregular subjunctive form of "pleuvoir" required after "bien que".

items.fr: Les ouvriers viendront réparer la fuite dès qu'ils pourront.
items.en: The workers will come fix the leak as soon as they can.
items.ipa: /le.z‿u.vʁi.je vjɛ̃.dʁɔ̃ ʁe.pa.ʁe la fɥit dɛ kil puʁ.ʁɔ̃/
items.notes: The plural "s" of "ouvriers" stays silent because the next word "viendront" begins with a consonant, so no liaison occurs.

items.fr: Mon voisin est plus bruyant que je ne le pensais.
items.en: My neighbor is noisier than I thought.
items.ipa: /mɔ̃ vwa.zɛ̃ ɛ ply bʁɥi.jɑ̃ kə ʒə nə lə pɑ̃.sɛ/
items.notes: The string of mute e's in "que je ne le" is barely pronounced in fast speech, but every one must still be written.

items.fr: C'est le locataire qui doit payer les petites réparations.
items.en: It is the tenant who has to pay for the small repairs.
items.ipa: /sɛ lə lɔ.ka.tɛʁ ki dwa pe.je le pə.tit ʁe.pa.ʁa.sjɔ̃/
items.notes: "c'est" is easy to confuse with "s'est" or "ses" since all three sound the same.

items.fr: Je doute que ce studio soit assez grand pour deux.
items.en: I doubt this studio is big enough for two.
items.ipa: /ʒə dut kə sə sty.djo swa a.se ɡʁɑ̃ puʁ dø/
items.notes: "soit" is the subjunctive of "être" required after "je doute que", not to be confused with "soi" or "sois".

items.fr: Quand nous aurons fini les travaux, nous inviterons nos amis.
items.en: When we have finished the renovations, we will invite our friends.
items.ipa: /kɑ̃ nu.z‿o.ʁɔ̃ fi.ni le tʁa.vo nu.z‿ɛ̃.vi.tə.ʁɔ̃ no.z‿a.mi/
items.notes: Three separate liaisons link "nous aurons", "nous inviterons", and "nos amis" with /z/ sounds.

items.fr: Il semble que les clés aient été oubliées sur la table.
items.en: It seems the keys were forgotten on the table.
items.ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə le kle ɛ.t‿e.te u.bli.je syʁ la tabl/
items.notes: "aient" is the subjunctive of "avoir", spelled with "-ent" though it is pronounced just like "est" or "es".

items.fr: Ses parents ont refait toute la toiture l'été dernier.
items.en: His parents redid the whole roof last summer.
items.ipa: /se pa.ʁɑ̃ ɔ̃ ʁə.fɛ tut la twa.tyʁ le.te dɛʁ.nje/
items.notes: "ses" (possessive) sounds the same as "ces" and "c'est" but has a different spelling and role.

items.fr: Nous cherchons un appartement où les charges sont incluses.
items.en: We are looking for an apartment where the utilities are included.
items.ipa: /nu ʃɛʁ.ʃɔ̃.z‿œ̃ na.paʁ.tə.mɑ̃ u le ʃaʁʒ sɔ̃.t‿ɛ̃.klyz/
items.notes: "où" keeps its accent because it means "where", unlike the conjunction "ou" meaning "or".

items.fr: Il vaudrait mieux que vous répariez la fenêtre avant l'hiver.
items.en: It would be better for you to fix the window before winter.
items.ipa: /il vo.dʁɛ mjø kə vu ʁe.pa.ʁje la fə.nɛtʁ a.vɑ̃ li.vɛʁ/
items.notes: The subjunctive ending "-iez" of "répariez" sounds close to the simple "-ez" ending, so it is easy to drop the extra "i".

items.fr: Les meubles que nous avons vendus étaient très anciens.
items.en: The furniture that we sold was very old.
items.ipa: /le mœbl kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ vɑ̃.dy e.tɛ tʁɛ.z‿ɑ̃.sjɛ̃/
items.notes: "vendus" takes a plural "s" to agree with "les meubles", the direct object placed before "avons vendu".

items.fr: La maison qu'ils ont achetée avait besoin de travaux.
items.en: The house they bought needed renovation work.
items.ipa: /la mɛ.zɔ̃ kil.z‿ɔ̃ aʃ.te.te a.vɛ bə.zwɛ̃ də tʁa.vo/
items.notes: "achetée" adds a silent feminine "e" to agree with "la maison", the preceding direct object of "ont acheté".
The final d of vend is silent, a common trap for this regular verb ending.

items.fr: S'il avait plu, nous n'aurions pas repeint la façade.
items.en: If it had rained, we would not have repainted the facade.
items.ipa: /sil a.vɛ ply nu no.ʁjɔ̃ pa ʁə.pɛ̃ la fa.sad/
items.notes: "si" elides to "s'" only before "il" or "ils", never before other pronouns like "elle".

items.fr: Bien qu'elle soit propriétaire, elle loue quand même une chambre.
items.en: Even though she is an owner, she still rents out a room.
items.ipa: /bjɛ̃ kɛl swa pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ ɛl lu kɑ̃ mɛm yn ʃɑ̃bʁ/
items.notes: "que" elides before "elle" to become "qu'elle", pronounced as one syllable.

items.fr: Les clés que le locataire nous a rendues étaient rouillées.
items.en: The keys that the tenant gave back to us were rusty.
items.ipa: /le kle kə lə lɔ.ka.tɛʁ nu.z‿a ʁɑ̃.dy e.tɛ ʁu.je/
items.notes: "rendues" agrees with the feminine plural "les clés", the direct object placed before the auxiliary "a rendu".

items.fr: Si j'avais su, je n'aurais jamais signé ce bail.
items.en: If I had known, I would never have signed this lease.
items.ipa: /si ʒa.vɛ sy ʒə no.ʁɛ ʒa.mɛ si.ɲe sə baj/
items.notes: "je" elides before the vowel of "avais" to form "j'avais", one of several elisions in this sentence.

items.fr: Il faudrait que le propriétaire fasse changer la chaudière.
items.en: The landlord would need to have the boiler changed.
items.ipa: /il fo.dʁɛ kə lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ fas ʃɑ̃.ʒe la ʃo.djɛʁ/
items.notes: "fasse" is the subjunctive form required after "il faudrait que", distinct from the indicative "fait" though both come from "faire".

items.fr: C'est le bruit des voisins du dessus qui l'empêche de dormir.
items.en: It is the noise from the upstairs neighbors that keeps him from sleeping.
items.ipa: /sɛ lə bʁɥi de vwa.zɛ̃ dy də.sy ki lɑ̃.pɛʃ də dɔʁ.miʁ/
items.notes: "le" elides to "l'" before the vowel of "empêche", merging into a single sound.

items.fr: Quoiqu'elle ait repeint tout le couloir, l'odeur de peinture persiste.
items.en: Although she repainted the whole hallway, the smell of paint lingers.
items.ipa: /kwa.kɛl ɛ ʁə.pɛ̃ tu lə ku.lwaʁ lo.dœʁ də pɛ̃.tyʁ pɛʁ.sist/
items.notes: "ait", the subjunctive of "avoir", sounds identical to "es", "est", and "ai" but is spelled differently.

items.fr: Les travaux que l'entreprise a entrepris coûtent plus cher que prévu.
items.en: The work that the company undertook costs more than expected.
items.ipa: /le tʁa.vo kə lɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz a ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁi kut ply ʃɛʁ kə pʁe.vy/
items.notes: "entrepris" stays unchanged for masculine plural agreement because the base form already ends in "s".

items.fr: Il aurait fallu qu'on repeigne la chambre avant l'arrivée du bébé.
items.en: The bedroom should have been repainted before the baby's arrival.
items.ipa: /il o.ʁɛ fa.ly kɔ̃ ʁə.pɛɲ la ʃɑ̃bʁ a.vɑ̃ la.ʁi.ve dy be.be/
items.notes: "que" elides before "on" to form "qu'on", and "repeigne" is the irregular subjunctive of "repeindre".

items.fr: La décoration qu'elle a choisie correspond parfaitement au salon.
items.en: The decor she chose matches the living room perfectly.
items.ipa: /la de.kɔ.ʁa.sjɔ̃ kɛl a ʃwa.zi kɔ.ʁɛs.pɔ̃ paʁ.fɛt.mɑ̃ o sa.lɔ̃/
items.notes: "choisie" adds a feminine "e" because the preceding direct object "que" refers to "la décoration".

items.fr: Quels que soient les travaux, le propriétaire doit être prévenu.
items.en: Whatever the work involved, the landlord must be informed.
items.ipa: /kɛl kə swa.t‿le tʁa.vo lə pʁɔ.pʁi.je.tɛʁ dwa.t‿ɛtʁ pʁe.və.ny/
items.notes: "Quels que soient" requires the plural subjunctive "soient", agreeing with the plural "les travaux".

items.fr: Si nous avions loué un logement plus calme, nous aurions mieux dormi.
items.en: If we had rented a quieter place, we would have slept better.
items.ipa: /si nu.z‿a.vjɔ̃ lwe œ̃ lɔʒ.mɑ̃ ply kalm nu.z‿o.ʁjɔ̃ mjø dɔʁ.mi/
items.notes: Liaison links "nous avions" and "nous aurions" with /z/ sounds not shown by any letter of "nous".

items.fr: Le marché est ouvert le samedi matin.
items.en: The market is open on Saturday morning.
items.notes: Liaison between est and ouvert adds a t sound that is not heard when est stands alone.
Je elides to j' before the vowel-initial verb achète.

items.fr: Elle choisit des tomates bien mûres.
items.notes: The final t in choisit is silent, easy to forget when writing.
Pèse needs a grave accent to mark the open e sound, a detail invisible in casual speech.

items.en: How much does this cheese cost?
items.notes: Combien contains two nasal vowels that are easy to under-articulate when writing quickly.

items.en: We are looking for yellow flowers.

items.fr: Vous voulez un kilo de carottes ?

items.notes: The unstressed e in de is a schwa that can fade in speech but must stay in writing.

items.fr: Ils achètent du pain à la boulangerie.
items.en: They buy bread at the bakery.
items.notes: Liaison between ils and achètent produces a z sound signaling the plural, not audible in il achète.

items.en: They look at the exotic fruits.

items.fr: Je prends deux kilos de pommes de terre.

items.fr: Le marchand rend la monnaie rapidement.
items.en: The merchant gives back the change quickly.
items.notes: Marchand, rend, and rapidement all contain nasal vowels that are easy to under-articulate when writing.
Lourde adds a feminine final e to agree with pastèque, a change not heard in speech.

items.fr: Les abricots sont chers cette semaine.
items.notes: Liaison between les and abricots adds a z sound marking the plural.

items.fr: On paie en espèces ou par carte.
items.en: We pay in cash or by card.
items.notes: Ou (or) has no accent, unlike its homophone où (where); context decides the spelling.

items.fr: Le client demande le prix des oranges.
items.en: The customer asks the price of the oranges.
items.ipa: /lə kli.jɑ̃ də.mɑ̃d lə pʁi de ɔ.ʁɑ̃ʒ/
items.notes: The final t in client is silent, a frequent spelling slip in dictée.

items.fr: La marchande sourit à ses clients.
items.en: The market woman smiles at her customers.
items.notes: À needs a grave accent to distinguish it from a (has), even though they sound the same.

items.fr: Les enfants aiment les fraises sucrées.
items.notes: Liaison between les and enfants adds a z that signals the plural article.

items.fr: Il y a beaucoup de monde au marché.
items.en: There are a lot of people at the market.
items.notes: The nasal vowel in monde is easy to under-pronounce, leading learners to drop the n when writing.

items.fr: Les pommes sont dans le panier.
items.en: The apples are in the basket.

items.fr: Elle porte un grand sac de courses.

items.ipa: /ɛl pɔʁt œ̃ gʁɑ̃ sak də kuʁs/
items.notes: The final d of grand is silent before a consonant, unlike in liaison contexts.
Poissonnier doubles the n, a spelling detail not obvious from pronunciation.

items.fr: Nous achetons du fromage de chèvre.
items.notes: Liaison links nous and achetons with a z sound absent from the written words individually.
The -ent ending of sentent is silent, matching the plural subject without being heard.

items.fr: Je voudrais un kilo de cerises.
items.en: I would like a kilo of cherries.
items.notes: The schwa in je and de often disappears in fast speech but must remain in writing.

items.fr: Le fromager coupe une tranche de fromage.
items.en: The cheesemonger cuts a slice of cheese.

items.notes: The -er ending of fromager is pronounced like é, a classic dictée confusion point.

items.fr: Les clients font la queue devant l'étal.
items.en: The customers wait in line in front of the stall.
items.ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ fɔ̃ la kø də.vɑ̃ le.tal/
items.notes: Le étal elides to l'étal before the vowel-initial noun.

items.fr: Elle met les légumes dans son sac.
items.en: She puts the vegetables in her bag.
items.ipa: /ɛl mɛ le le.gym dɑ̃ sɔ̃ sak/
items.notes: Son (her) sounds identical to sont (are), so only meaning distinguishes the spelling.

items.fr: Le vendeur crie les prix du jour.
items.en: The seller calls out the day's prices.
items.ipa: /lə vɑ̃.dœʁ kʁi le pʁi dy ʒuʁ/
items.notes: The final x in prix is silent, easy to omit or misplace in dictée.
The circumflex on goûtons is silent but required in spelling, marking a lost historical s.
Vendent carries a nasal vowel followed by a silent -ent ending, both easy to misspell.
Liaison between deux and euros adds a z sound not present when deux stands alone.

items.fr: Ce raisin vient du sud de la France.
items.en: This grape comes from the south of France.
items.ipa: /sə ʁɛ.zɛ̃ vjɛ̃ dy syd də la fʁɑ̃s/
items.notes: Raisin ends in a nasal vowel that beginners often spell with an extra n.
Liaison after prix surfaces a z sound that the silent written x does not suggest.
Œufs in the plural loses the f sound heard in singular œuf, an irregular spelling-to-sound trap.
The final r of boucher is silent, following the standard -er ending pattern.

items.en: We are choosing a good melon.
items.notes: Un, bon, and melon all contain nasal vowels that are easy to under-articulate in dictée.

items.fr: Les asperges sont vertes et fines.
items.en: The asparagus are green and thin.
items.notes: Vertes and fines both add silent feminine plural endings to agree with asperges.

items.fr: Le marché ferme à treize heures.
items.en: The market closes at one o'clock.
items.notes: À carries an accent grave to distinguish it from a, though both are pronounced the same.

items.en: I love the smell of fresh bread.
items.notes: Both je and le elide before vowel-initial words, giving j'aime and l'odeur.

items.fr: Elle porte des sacs très lourds.
items.en: She is carrying very heavy bags.
items.notes: The final ds in lourds is completely silent, only visible in the written plural form.

items.fr: Les touristes visitent le marché local.
items.en: The tourists visit the local market.
items.notes: The silent -ent ending on visitent shows the plural subject without any audible change.

items.fr: Le vieux marchand connaît tous ses clients.
items.en: The old merchant knows all his customers.
items.ipa: /lə vjø maʁ.ʃɑ̃ kɔ.nɛ tu se kli.jɑ̃/
items.notes: Connaît keeps a circumflex accent on the i, a silent mark that must not be forgotten.

items.fr: Nous prenons un citron et deux oranges.
items.en: We are taking a lemon and two oranges.
items.notes: Citron ends in a nasal vowel often mis-transcribed with an extra n.

items.fr: Les champignons sont dans une petite boîte.
items.en: The mushrooms are in a small box.
items.notes: Boîte keeps a circumflex on the i, a silent accent that changes nothing in pronunciation but is required in spelling.

items.fr: Elle achète des épices pour la soupe.
items.en: She buys spices for the soup.
items.notes: Liaison between des and épices produces an audible z marking the plural.

items.fr: Le marché est près de l'église.
items.en: The market is near the church.
items.notes: La église elides to l'église because the noun begins with a vowel sound.
The silent -ent ending on goûtent signals a plural subject that cannot be heard.

items.fr: La marchande pèse les pommes une à une.
items.en: The market woman weighs the apples one by one.
items.ipa: /la maʁ.ʃɑ̃d pɛz le pɔm yn a yn/
items.notes: À needs its accent grave even though it sounds exactly like a (has).

items.fr: Les clients paient et partent vite.
items.en: The customers pay and leave quickly.
items.notes: Et (and) is a homophone of est (is); only the sentence meaning tells you which to write.

items.fr: Hier, j'ai acheté des fraises au marché.
items.en: Yesterday, I bought strawberries at the market.
items.ipa: /jɛʁ ʒe aʃ.te de fʁɛz o maʁ.ʃe/
items.notes: Acheté ends in a sound identical to acheter and achetez, so the ending must be chosen by grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Nous avons choisi les meilleurs fromages.
items.notes: Liaison between nous and avons adds a z sound not visible in either word alone.

items.fr: Elle a payé avec sa carte bancaire.
items.en: She paid with her bank card.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pɛ.je a.vɛk sa kaʁt bɑ̃.kɛʁ/
items.notes: Payé sounds the same as payer and payez, so the past participle ending relies on grammar, not sound.

items.fr: Ils sont allés au marché tôt le matin.
items.en: They went to the market early in the morning.
items.ipa: /il sɔ̃ a.le o maʁ.ʃe to lə ma.tɛ̃/
items.notes: Allés takes a silent plural s to agree with ils because it uses the auxiliary être.

items.fr: Le vendeur a pesé les tomates.
items.notes: Pesé ends in the same sound as peser, a frequent past participle confusion.

items.fr: Nous allons acheter du pain demain.
items.en: We are going to buy bread tomorrow.
items.notes: Liaison between nous and allons produces a z sound that signals the plural subject.

items.fr: Elle va goûter le fromage de chèvre.
items.en: She is going to taste the goat cheese.
items.ipa: /ɛl va gu.te lə fʁɔ.maʒ də ʃɛvʁ/
items.notes: The circumflex on goûter is silent but must be written, marking a historical lost s.

items.fr: Vous avez trouvé des fruits mûrs.
items.notes: Trouvé sounds identical to trouver and trouvez, so only grammar tells you which ending to write.

items.fr: Les enfants ont mangé toutes les cerises.
items.en: The children ate all the cherries.
items.notes: Ont (have) is a homophone of on (one), distinguished only by grammatical context.

items.fr: On a acheté beaucoup de légumes.
items.en: We bought a lot of vegetables.
items.notes: On sounds like ont, so writers must rely on meaning to choose the right spelling.

items.fr: Où as-tu trouvé ces belles fleurs ?
items.en: Where did you find these beautiful flowers?
items.ipa: /u a ty tʁu.ve se bɛl flœʁ/
items.notes: Où (where) carries an accent to distinguish it from ou (or), though both sound identical.

items.fr: Elle a demandé le prix des poires.
items.en: She asked the price of the pears.
items.ipa: /ɛl a də.mɑ̃.de lə pʁi de pwaʁ/
items.notes: Demandé ends the same as demander, a common past participle spelling trap.

items.fr: Nous avons marché longtemps entre les étals.
items.en: We walked for a long time between the stalls.
items.notes: Longtemps contains two nasal vowels and a silent final s, easy to misspell.

items.fr: Ils ont goûté les olives avant d'acheter.
items.en: They tasted the olives before buying.
items.notes: De acheter elides to d'acheter before the vowel-initial verb.

items.fr: Le marchand a donné la monnaie à Paul.
items.en: The merchant gave the change to Paul.
items.ipa: /lə maʁ.ʃɑ̃ a dɔ.ne la mɔ.nɛ a pɔl/
items.notes: The sentence contains both a (has) and à (to), which sound identical but are spelled differently.

items.fr: Elle a pris deux kilos de pommes.
items.en: She took two kilos of apples.
items.ipa: /ɛl a pʁi dø ki.lo də pɔm/
items.notes: The final s of the past participle pris is silent, easy to drop in dictée.

items.fr: On va négocier le prix du poisson.

items.ipa: /ɔ̃ va ne.gɔ.sje lə pʁi dy pwa.sɔ̃/
items.notes: On and poisson both carry nasal vowels that beginners often under-pronounce when writing.

items.fr: Les clients ont fait la queue longtemps.

items.ipa: /le kli.jɑ̃ ɔ̃ fɛ la kø lɔ̃.tɑ̃/
items.notes: Ont (have) must not be confused with its homophone on (one), a frequent dictée error.

items.fr: Nous avons mis les fruits dans un sac.

items.fr: Elle est arrivée tôt pour choisir les meilleurs produits.

items.fr: Ils vont vendre des fleurs demain matin.

items.fr: On a payé en espèces au marchand.

items.fr: Elle a comparé les prix entre deux étals.

items.fr: On va acheter des asperges fraîches.

items.fr: Il range ses outils dans le fond du garage.

items.fr: Mon vieux sac est vraiment lourd.

items.en: I am buying a new umbrella today.

items.en: My phone is staying at the hotel.

items.fr: Ma montre tombe souvent dans l'herbe.

items.fr: J'ai un joli collier en argent.

items.fr: J'ai un beau sac en cuir.

items.en: I really like this old watch.

items.fr: Le sac que tu portes est joli.

items.fr: Ils sont partis sans leurs valises.

items.fr: La valise que j'ai achetée est très lourde.
items.en: The suitcase I bought is very heavy.
